stem.text: The functions \( f \) and \( h \) are continuous for all real numbers. The function \( g \) is continuous except at \( x = 2 \), where \( \lim_{x \to 2^-} g(x) = 1 \) and \( \lim_{x \to 2^+} g(x) = 4 \). The known values are \( f(0) = 1 \), \( f(1) = 1 \), \( f(2) = 3 \), \( f(3) = 4 \), \( f(4) = 2 \), \( g(0) = 4 \), \( g(1) = 4 \), \( g(3) = 0 \), \( g(4) = 4 \), \( h(0) = 3 \), \( h(1) = 4 \), \( h(2) = 4 \), \( h(3) = 1 \), \( h(4) = 2 \). Find the value of \( \lim_{x \to 2^+} \left[ 3h(f(x)) + 2g(h(x)) + 3f(g(x)) \right] \).

worked_solution.text: Record the limits. As \( x \to 2^+ \), \( g(x) \to 4 \), and \( f \) and \( h \) are continuous, so their limits are their values at 2.

The expression is a sum of constant multiples of three composites. In each composite the outer function is continuous at the limit of the inner one, so \( \lim_{x \to 2^+} h(f(x)) = h(3) = 1 \), \( \lim_{x \to 2^+} g(h(x)) = g(4) = 4 \), \( \lim_{x \to 2^+} f(g(x)) = f(4) = 2 \).
Apply the sum and constant multiple theorems: \( (3)(1) + (2)(4) + (3)(2) = 17 \).
